title: About
text:
I am an economist and Senior Researcher at Red de Estudios para el Desarrollo (REDES), a Peruvian public policy think tank. I manage a team of research assistants and work on youth employment, urban poverty, inflation, food insecurity and public transport.
My work starts with data: microdata from national household, employment, education and energy surveys, analysed with impact evaluation methods (difference-in-differences, regression discontinuity, instrumental variables) and data science tools in Stata, Python and R. I want that evidence to reach the public debate, which is why I write a regular column for El Comercio and present findings at universities across Peru.

title: Youth unemployment in Peru
text:
What the data tell us

Unemployment is only part of the problem: in Peru, many young people who do work hold informal, low-productivity jobs. This indicator is best read alongside youth informality and the share of young people not in employment, education or training.
For a fuller analysis, see the study Policies to improve youth labour market entry in Peru and the column Más oportunidades para los jóvenes (in Spanish).
